title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: makers can build declarative agents with flexible layouts and rich UX components
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says existing agent blocking and user access controls are not documented as governing these agents, despite Microsoft's documented organization-wide scope. The roadmap facts and control paths are accurate, but the licensing model also understates the published general entitlement for building declarative agents.

claims.quote: Microsoft CoPilot (Microsoft 365):  Makers can build DA's with Flexible layouts and rich UX components

claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/overview-declarative-agent for the definition; its configuration list includes instructions, knowledge and capabilities such as actions.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block reaches the agent blocking control.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access controls which users or groups access agents and plugins.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins. Select who can access agents and plugins within your organization.

claims.claim: User access defaults to All users.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: Blocking is an agent-level control, not a control specifically documented for this layouts feature.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
